subject: Reranker integration & evaluation — SDK, auth, routing
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Amit Desai <amit@searchly.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Reranker integration & evaluation — SDK, auth, routing

Thanks for the call this morning, Amit — good discussion. Quick recap and concrete asks so we keep momentum: 

Key takeaways
- Searchly is evaluating a reranker layer on top of your current lexical + sparse results. Goal: raise precision@10 and NDCG for commercial queries without increasing 95th latency beyond 120ms.
- Primary integration path: Redwood SDK (server-side) -> Redwood API/Routing -> reranker model variant -> structured outputs that include a relevance score + provenance token spans.

Open technical questions we need answered from your side
1) Auth: do you prefer us to use an API-key per environment or do you require OAuth2 client-credentials? Any IP allowlist / mTLS constraints?
2) Routing & region: where will inference traffic originate (us-east-1 vs eu-west-1)? We can pin routing to region or fall back to cheaper variants — want to know latency constraints.
3) Embeddings/reranker signal: what embedding dimensionality are you using for recalls today (e.g., 768/1024)? Any quantization already applied?
4) Eval data: could you share a 500–1,000 query gold set + current ranking logs (anonymized) for offline NDCG/MRR evaluation?

Proposed next steps (please confirm owners & dates)
- Searchly: share sample eval set and any PII redaction rules by Fri 2026-12-03. (Amit / Rahul)
- Redwood: provide SDK quickstart + auth options and a 60-minute technical workshop for engineers by Tue 2026-12-08. (Ben)
- Joint: agree on acceptance criteria (metric targets & latency SLO) following initial offline run. (Priya / Amit)

Attachments: MAP-Searchly.pdf (brief mutual action plan)

Thanks — I’m cc'ing Ben for tech follow-ups and Rishi for success criteria.

—
Priya Natarajan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: MAP-Searchly.pdf (PDF)]

From: Amit Desai <amit@searchly.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Cc: Rahul Sharma <rahul@searchly.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T11:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Reranker integration & evaluation — SDK, auth, routing

Thanks Priya — great summary. Quick answers from our side: 

Auth & infra
- We prefer OAuth2 client-credentials for production. For PoC, API keys are fine (we can issue ephemeral keys). No mTLS required today but we do IP allowlisting for our service-to-service traffic.

Region & traffic
- Most traffic originates from us-west-2 and us-east-1. Latency budget per user request is 120ms p95 (includes recall + rerank).

Embeddings/reranker setup
- Current embedding dim: 768 (float32), no quantization in production. We store dense vectors in Faiss HNSW.

Eval data
- I can share an anonymized sample set (1,200 queries) and click logs — will scrub PII. Rahul will drop the files into the Drive link you shared by EOD Thu 2026-12-02.

Question for Ben: what is the recommended auth flow for the SDK if Searchly requires OAuth for prod but wants quick PoC? Do we need an intermediate token-exchange?

— Amit
Head of Search, Searchly

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Amit Desai <amit@searchly.ai>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T08:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Reranker integration & evaluation — SDK, auth, routing

Amit — quick tech notes on the SDK/auth/routing pieces and how they map to evaluation: 

1) Auth patterns (recommended)
- PoC: use Redwood API key scoped to a test project. We return short-lived bearer tokens to your side if you prefer not to embed keys.
- Prod: OAuth2 client-credentials + token introspection. Typical pattern: Searchly auth server performs client-credentials grant with Redwood Auth; Redwood issues a scoped token bound to your project. No mandatory token-exchange required on your side, but many customers do an internal exchange so they never store third-party secrets.

2) Routing & model variants
- You can configure routing rules by region and latency target. For example: prefer reranker-xx-small in us-west-2 for <50ms budgets, fallback to reranker-small in us-east-1 for cost-optimized runs. We support automatic fallback to a compatible model variant if the pinned model is unavailable.

3) Structured outputs & tool-calling
- Reranker returns per-candidate structured JSON: {"score": float, "excerpts": [ {"start":int, "end":int, "source_id":string} ], "signal_info": {"embed_sim":float, "lexical_score":float} }
- If you use tool-calling, we can surface argument schemas so your downstream services can consume ranked candidates deterministically. I attached a tiny SDK snippet showing how to request structured outputs and read the score field.

4) Embeddings and rerank config
- For 768-dim embeddings, we recommend L2-normalized dot-product similarity and evaluating top_k in {5, 10, 20}. In practice we see diminishing returns past top_k=20 for commercial query mixes.

5) Evaluation metrics & instrumentation (initial suggestions)
- Offline: NDCG@10, MRR@10, Recall@k, pairwise win-rate vs baseline. Use stratified slices by query intent (transactional vs navigational).
- Online (PoC): A/B with interleaving at traffic ratio 10/90; monitor p95 latency, downstream click-through uplift, and human-blind relevance judgments on a 500-sample set.

Attachment: rerank_sdk_snippet.py (shows request/response parsing for structured outputs).

If you want, we can run an initial offline evaluation on your 1,200-query set and return a scoreboard (NDCG/MRR) and recommended top_k per slice. I estimate ~48–72 hours turnaround once we have the data and baseline ranks.

—Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: rerank_sdk_snippet.py (Python)]

From: Amit Desai <amit@searchly.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Cc: Rahul Sharma <rahul@searchly.ai>
Date: 2026-11-30T10:10:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Reranker integration & evaluation — SDK, auth, routing

Thanks Ben — that clarifies a lot. A couple of follow-ups before we hand off to our infra team: 

Evaluation specifics
- Acceptance criteria: we want at least +7% NDCG@10 vs baseline on the head query set and no more than +5ms median latency and +15ms p95 latency (end-to-end including recall). Are those numbers feasible?
- For human eval: what rubric do you use for relevance judgments? Can you share a sample annotation guideline?

Top_k behavior
- We currently surface top 10 to product page. Are you recommending returning top_k=20 for reranking internally then truncating to 10 for display? Would that help surface reorders that are useful?

Data sharing
- Rahul is uploading the sample set now. We'll include a small baseline rank column. Any preferred CSV schema?

— Amit

From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-11-30T15:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Reranker integration & evaluation — SDK, auth, routing

Amit — thanks for the details and the eval/latency targets. Quick answers and updated mutual action plan below: 

Feasibility on acceptance criteria
- +7% NDCG@10: reasonable as an initial target for head traffic slices; we'll run the offline baseline and confirm. If the baseline is very high already, we may adjust to relative improvement thresholds.
- Latency: +5ms median and +15ms p95 are aggressive but plausible depending on your recall latency and nearest-neighbor search setup. We'll instrument an end-to-end measurement in the PoC.

Human eval rubric (attached)
- We'll provide a 1-page annotation guideline: binary relevance + 3-point utility scale + a short note field for edge cases. That will be included with the offline scoreboard.

Top_k recommendation
- Yes — rerank on top_k=20 internally, then display top 10 after rerank is common because it lets the reranker consider more context and surface a better reorder. We'll include both internal top_k and display_k when we report.

CSV schema for uploads
- Preferred columns: query_id, query_text, doc_id, baseline_rank, doc_text (or doc_excerpt), timestamp. If including embeddings, separate file is fine.

Updated next steps & owners
- Searchly (Amit/Rahul): upload anonymized eval set to Drive and confirm schema by 2026-12-02 (Rahul).
- Redwood (Ben): run offline evaluation on the provided set and return NDCG/MRR scoreboard + recommended top_k by 2026-12-04. Attach human eval guidelines and SDK snippet. (Ben)
- Joint: 60-minute workshop to review findings and plan PoC integration on 2026-12-09 — please confirm attendee list. (Priya to schedule)

Attachments: human_eval_guideline.txt (I'll upload separately), MAP-Searchly.pdf

If that timeline works I’ll send a calendar invite for 12/09 and include an agenda (offline findings, integration plan, canary approach).

Thanks —
Priya
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
